segments.text: Priya runs a one-chair nail studio. About one visit in twenty-five is a no-show, and charging a regular who had a bad day feels wrong. HoldMySpot holds the fee, not the grudge.
I create my studio in a few seconds. A name, my first name, no password.
Here is my cancellation policy, in plain words. I keep it.
PayPal is connected to the sandbox, so the money is test money. Everything else you see is live.
And this is the booking link I would put in my bio.
A client opens it, picks a time, and approves a twenty dollar hold in her own PayPal. It is not a charge. It only reserves the money. This is the real PayPal sandbox, with a real test buyer.
Back in my studio, the visit is on the schedule, with a real PayPal authorization behind it.
Later, she texts: her kid was sick all night and she cannot make it.
The front desk reads the reason, checks my policy, and proposes: excused, no charge. It cannot move money. I tap, and the hold is released on PayPal.
Alex booked the same way, and does not show. The clock skips ahead, the front desk asks if Alex arrived, and I say no.
One tap charges the hold we already have. Twenty dollars, captured.
Alex apologises, so one more tap refunds it.
The ledger keeps every PayPal authorization, capture and refund id, next to the exact request behind it.
The empty chair gets refilled, the regular keeps her dignity, and Priya gets paid when it is fair. HoldMySpot.
